title: Sandboxed eval lifecycle and config-delta gating for customer-specific quality checks
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Model or configuration changes (runtime flags, quantization profile, batching policy, routing rules) can cause regressions that are visible only for a customer's unique data distribution. For Dedicated and Private customers we must provide a way to run isolated, privacy-preserving customer-specific eval suites tied to config deltas so that rollouts do not degrade perceived quality.

Proposed solution: Build a sandboxed eval lifecycle that runs on ephemeral, customer-scoped execution environments. Key features: (1) config-delta triggers: when a model binary or serving config changes, run an eval job scoped to affected customers; (2) golden-set layering: customers provide an encrypted golden-set (optionally masked/hashed) which is run only inside the sandbox; (3) differential scoring & fingerprinting: compare baseline and candidate using signal-aware metrics and keep cryptographic fingerprints to detect tampering; (4) privacy controls: optional local-only eval runners for Private deployments, KMS-wrapped corpora for Dedicated, no raw-corpus persistence in hosted; (5) gating rules: automatic canary block when customer-specific quality drops exceed thresholds or trigger manual review; (6) console & API: per-customer eval templates, results summary, and audit trail for compliance.

Why different from existing eval work: this ticket focuses on lifecycle orchestration (triggering on config deltas and model swaps), runtime isolation for customer artifacts, and strict data minimization rather than generic regression monitoring across tenants.

Constraints/assumptions: we will rely on existing runner infra for ephemeral workloads (ENG) and use KMS/HSM integrations already planned in the Private team's roadmap. We must account for cost per eval and provide a clear opt-in model for customers.
acceptance_criteria: Config-delta hook implemented: model or serving-config change events can start a customer-scoped eval job
Sandbox runner: eval jobs execute in an ephemeral environment with network controls and are fully torn down after completion
Customer artifact handling: flow for customer to upload golden-sets encrypted with KMS, with option to provide hashed/masked versions
Differential report: baseline vs candidate metrics generated automatically and attached to the rollout event
Gating: rollout automation can be configured to block or flag rollouts when customer-specific quality delta exceeds thresholds
Privacy rules enforced: no raw customer corpus persisted in hosted; Private deployments support local-only evaluation with no telemetry export
Console UI: per-customer eval template and results summary visible to authorized users with appropriate RBAC
Audit trail: every eval run has an immutable audit record with fingerprints and summary stored for retention window

notes: Cost model: rough estimate 1-3 GPU-hours per medium-sized customer eval; must surface cost estimate in console before run
Consider providing a simulated dry-run mode that uses smaller slices of the golden set for quick gating
Retention: default 30 days for aggregated results, 0 days for raw customer inputs in hosted unless customer opts in
Fallback: if sandbox runner fails, rollout should continue unless gating is set to block by policy (configurable per customer)
